test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 3 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The population of a town 2 years ago was 8000. If the population growth rate is 30% per annum. What will the population after 1 year ?
solution:
**Given:**

The population of a town 2 years ago was 8000

If the population growth rate is 30% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Population after increased = P x ((100+R))/(100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ The population of town before 2 years= 8000

⇒ The population of town before 1 years= P x ((100+R))/(100)= 8000 x ((100+30))/(100)= 80 x 130= 10400

⇒ The population of town present= P x ((100+R))/(100)= 10400 x ((100+30))/(100)= 104 x 130= 13520

⇒ The population of town after 1 years= P x ((100+R))/(100)= 13520 x ((100+30))/(100)= 135.2 x 130= 17576

**Hence, The population of the town after 1 year is 17576.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Here, 30% = 3/10 i.e. 3 units increase out of 10 units.

Total increase = 13/10 units

Let the present population of town = P

⇒ 8000 × 13/10 × 13/10 = P

⇒ P = 13520

Population of after 1 year = 13520 × 13/10 = 17576
